# Cents that depend on the math library: fdlibm (StrictMath) against glibc 2.43

What was run and why: how often two math libraries, each within an ulp, put a money amount on
different cents, at table sizes of 10^9 and 10^10 rows (flips.c), and how Spark rounds such
amounts (round-check.sql). A count of rows, not a timing.

Date: 25 November 2026
Host: laptop, AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX PRO 370, Linux 7.0.0-44-generic, glibc 2.43, gcc 15.2.0 (Ubuntu 15.2.0-16ubuntu1)
fdlibm: reference/fdlibm-5.3's e_pow.c and e_exp.c, built as flips.c's header says; on its first
      2,000,000 rows they equal StrictMath on JDK 25.0.5.1+2-1-26.04.1-Ubuntu (FlipsCheck.java:
      "2000000 rows, 0 fdlibm results differ from StrictMath")
Spark: Apache Spark 4.3.0 (git revision 98bc0212c94), spark-4.3.0-bin-hadoop3.tgz from
      dlcdn.apache.org, checked against Apache's SHA-512; spark-sql --master 'local[1]' -S -f
      round-check.sql on JDK 21.0.13.1 and on JDK 25.0.5.1, with the same output on both
Command: OMP_NUM_THREADS=8 ./flips 1000000000 2> rows-1e9.txt; OMP_NUM_THREADS=8 ./flips 10000000000

## flips.c

rows 1000000000, glibc 2.43
pow: libraries differ on 91835075 rows; cents differ on 22 from the exact value, on 30 from the shortest decimal
exp: libraries differ on 97352211 rows; cents differ on 49 from the exact value, on 59 from the shortest decimal

rows 10000000000, glibc 2.43
pow: libraries differ on 918324706 rows; cents differ on 253 from the exact value, on 291 from the shortest decimal
exp: libraries differ on 973504152 rows; cents differ on 439 from the exact value, on 417 from the shortest decimal

## round-check.sql on Spark 4.3.0 (JDK 21; JDK 25 printed the same)
## columns: fn, spark_value, spark_cents, glibc_value, glibc_cents; then round_below,
## round_above, bround_below

exp	1.6393330040499997E8	1.639333004E8	1.63933300405E8	1.6393330041E8
pow	6.88535397445E8	6.8853539745E8	6.885353974449999E8	6.8853539744E8
2.447161233E7	2.447161233E7	2.447161232E7

## Reading

- The two libraries' doubles differ on about 9% of rows (pow 9.2%, exp 9.7%), so a join, a
  GROUP BY or an equality test on these computed amounts sees a different value on that share.
- The cents differ far more rarely, since a cent boundary must fall between the two doubles: on
  10^9 rows 30 (pow) and 59 (exp) rows when rounding as Spark does, from the shortest decimal;
  on 10^10 rows 291 and 417. The count grows with the table, about ten times for ten times the
  rows. From the exact value, the counts are 22 and 49, then 253 and 439.
- Spark's round() rounds the shortest decimal of the double: round(24471612.324999999D, 2) is
  24471612.33, as is round(24471612.325000003D, 2). So a row can differ in its double and still
  not in its cents; the counts above follow that rule.
- Two rows checked end to end on Spark: 874,292.44 * exp(0.1342 * 39) gives 163,933,300.40 on
  Spark and 163,933,300.41 from glibc's double; 857,486.34 * power(1.1820, 40) gives
  688,535,397.45 on Spark and 688,535,397.44 from glibc's double. Which C library and rounding
  rule another engine uses is not measured here.
